title: Filtration quotients with genuine completed integral models
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Module sheaves, sheaf tensor products, derived categories and cohomology are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and $Q:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=\mathcal C_X[1/\varpi]$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. A rational module sheaf is constructible when on a finite locally closed stratification it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Every constructible $E_X$-module sheaf $F$ has a finite filtration $0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F$ with quotients $F_k/F_{k-1}\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$, where $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$ is a qcqs open immersion, $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ is a reduced closed immersion, and $L_k$ is a lisse $E_{S_k}$-module sheaf. Each $S_k$ is again noetherian finite-dimensional with $\ell$ invertible. There are constructible integral sheaves $N_k$ on $S_k$ and $M_k=v_{k!}(t_k)_*N_k$ on $X$, whose stratum models are $B_S\otimes_A P$ with $P$ finitely presented, with
$$E_{S_k}\otimes_{B_{S_k}}N_k\cong L_k,\quad M_k[0]\in\mathcal C_X,\quad E_X\otimes_{B_X}M_k\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k.$$
Membership includes completeness and compatible etale-origin witnesses, not just ordinary internal-module constructibility. The last comparison is induced by the sequential localization colimit and the actual exact open/closed module functors [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], with the ring restrictions of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Also every lisse $E_X$-sheaf has such a constructible $B_X$ lattice in degree zero [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-e-constructible-integral-lattice]. Finite free continuous $E$ models are identified with the finite constant models for the pulled condensed ring $C(-,E)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], only for applying the sheaf filtration [lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration].

source.place: Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.10; Proposition 6.8.11(3); Lemma 6.8.13 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), finite-stratum reduction, pp. 60-62

proof.text: Use the canonical coefficient isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] to write $B_T=A_T=C(|-|,A)$ and $E_T=C(|-|,E)$ on $X$ and its locally closed subschemes. These isomorphisms preserve constant sections, localization and immersion restriction. Nonarchimedean balls separate points and are clopen, so $E$ is totally disconnected. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations], the pulled condensed ring for $C(-,E)$ is this continuous coefficient ring, compatibly with the integral-to-field map. The internal/sectionwise module equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] preserves the underlying sheaves. Thus a local finite free continuous model $E_T^a$ becomes precisely the finite constant model $p_T^*\underline E\otimes_E E^a$, and conversely. We use this identification solely to apply the finite-model filtration, then regard all its sheaves and functors as sectionwise module sheaves.

The minimal-closed-subset property of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] rules out an infinite strictly descending chain of closed subsets of $X$, so its underlying space is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration] to $F$ through Step 1. It gives $\varnothing=V_0\subset\cdots\subset V_m=X$, reduced closed $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$, qcqs $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$, and the monic counit-image filtration $F_k=v_{k!}v_k^*F$ with $F_k/F_{k-1}\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$, where $L_k=t_k^*(F|_{V_k})$ has finite constant local models. A finitely presented module over the field $E$ has a finite basis; its corresponding local model is $E_{S_k}^a$. Hence each $L_k$ is lisse in the required continuous sense.

source.place: Definition 6.8.6 and the filtration used in Lemma 6.8.13; topological refinement: Stacks Tag 09Y5, topology.tex, lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification

proof.text: Check the geometric hypotheses before taking lattices. The immersions $V_k\to X$ and $S_k\to X$ are locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]; [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes their sources locally Noetherian. Every subset of the Noetherian space $|X|$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], so both sources are quasi-compact and therefore Noetherian schemes. For a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of either locally closed source, taking closures in $X$ gives a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets: intersecting each closure with the source recovers the original subset. This bounds their dimensions by $\dim X$. Finally a local-ring homomorphism sends a unit to a unit, so invertibility of $\ell$ restricts to both sources. The open complements of $t_k$ are qcqs as already supplied by the filtration lemma.

source.place: Geometric hypotheses of the finite-stratum reduction; Stacks Tags 01T5 (morphisms.tex, lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); dimension and unit checks written out

proof.text: For each $k$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-e-constructible-integral-lattice] on the scheme $S_k$ verified in Step 3. It gives a continuous-constructible $B_{S_k}$-module $N_k$ with $E_{S_k}\otimes_{B_{S_k}}N_k\cong L_k$. Its finite-stratum models are exactly $B_S\otimes_A P$ with $P$ finitely presented; no global local-freeness of $N_k$ is asserted. The same cited lemma applied directly on $X$ proves the additional assertion about every lisse $E_X$-sheaf.

Set $P_k=(t_k)_*N_k$ and $M_k=v_{k!}P_k$, using the actual module functors. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-model-open-closed-pieces] first on $V_k$, with closed part $S_k$, lattice $N_k$ there and zero on its complementary open. It proves that $P_k$ is continuous-constructible on $V_k$. Apply it again on $X$, with open part $V_k$, lattice $P_k$ there and zero on the closed complement. It proves that $M_k$ is continuous-constructible on $X$ and supplies the ordinary scalar-extension comparisons for both functors. Zero is an allowed integral model, represented by the finitely presented scalar module $0$; the zero choices impose no additional support assumption. The coefficient identifications are those fixed in Step 1, and the schemes satisfy the lemma's hypotheses by Step 3.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, finite-stratum pieces; ordinary open/closed integral-model lemma

proof.text: The complex $M_k[0]$ is bounded, has $M_k$ as its sole possibly nonzero cohomology sheaf, and all its cohomology sheaves have the finite-stratum scalar models established in Step 5. Apply condition (iii) implies (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] on $X$. Thus $M_k[0]\in\mathcal C_X$, including derived completeness, a uniformly bounded constructible reduction tower, and compatible etale-origin witnesses. In particular this is membership in the completed category of the statement, rather than just constructibility in the ordinary module category. This argument also puts each lattice $N_k[0]$ in the corresponding completed category on $S_k$, when desired.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), using the completed-coefficient and compatible-witness characterization

proof.text:
Verify the normalization of the scalar comparison rather than choosing an abstract isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-module-colimit], for any $B_T$-module $H$ its ordinary localization is the colimit of $H\xrightarrow{\varpi}H\xrightarrow{\varpi}\cdots$, with the map from stage $n\geq0$ given by $h\mapsto\varpi^{-n}\otimes h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], $(t_k)_*$ commutes with this small filtered colimit on the qcqs scheme $V_k$, and $v_{k!}$ commutes with it because it is a left adjoint. Their linearity sends the transition $\varpi$ to $\varpi$. Consequently the colimit comparisons give
$$E_X\otimes_{B_X}v_{k!}(t_k)_*N_k\ \cong\ v_{k!}(t_k)_*(E_{S_k}\otimes_{B_{S_k}}N_k).$$
On every stage both the composite comparison and the separate open/closed comparisons send a local section $h$ to the image of $\varpi^{-n}\otimes h$ under these same functors. The colimit universal property therefore makes them equal; the ring restrictions are precisely those of Step 1. Exactness of the actual open and closed module functors is part of the cited open-closed lemma, so these are the same functors as in the sheaf filtration. Compose with the lattice isomorphism from Step 4 to obtain $E_X\otimes_{B_X}M_k\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$. Together with Steps 2 and 6 this proves every required clause.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(2) and Lemma 6.8.13; Stacks Tags 09BM, 03DI, 03DJ, 0738 for the actual module functors and their colimits
